clue.text: Stress Musk’s content to follow international court (5)

indicators.note: a word's content is what sits inside its outer letters
the US comes after the ICT

annotation.surface: A complaint that Elon Musk's posts are now trailing an international court case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as social-media posts; here it means the letters inside MUSK. An ictus is the stress on a syllable in verse.
annotation.definitionFit: In prosody the ictus is the stress or beat falling on a syllable.

clue.text: Causes of anxiety including money for everyone (6)

blocks.note: inc. is the abbreviation for including

annotation.surface: A worry that a universal cash handout will itself cause anxiety.
annotation.walkthrough: UBI, universal basic income, is a proposed payment to every citizen. Incubi are nightmare demons, so figuratively things that weigh on the mind.
annotation.definitionFit: An incubus is an oppressive burden or nightmare, so incubi are causes of anxiety.

clue.text: No longer going potty? (6-7)

blocks.note: the surface hears 'no longer going mad'; the setter means a child who has stopped using something
not the slang for crazy but the child's pot, which a trained toddler has left behind for the lavatory

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether a person has regained their sanity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going potty' is British slang for going mad, which is the reading the surface pushes; the literal potty is the child's one.
annotation.definitionFit: Read literally, the clue describes a toddler who has graduated from a potty to the lavatory, which is exactly what training achieves.

clue.text: Obsessive admirer daughters tolerate (5)

blocks.note: a stan is an obsessive fan, from the Eminem song

annotation.surface: A parent wondering whether the daughters can put up with a superfan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obsessive admirer' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it only supplies STAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly heard in negatives: someone who can't bear a noise says they can't abide or put up with it.

clue.text: Back away from angry bluebottle, finally free after the setter’s knocked over lab equipment (10)

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so I'M turns round
the back letter goes away from CROSS

bluebottle is old slang for a policeman, from the blue uniform

annotation.surface: Someone backing away from a furious fly, then accidentally knocking over the lab kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottle' is set up as the fly; in crosswords it is a police officer. 'Back away from' reads as retreating, but it cuts the back letter off 'angry'.
annotation.definitionFit: A microscope is a standard piece of laboratory equipment.

annotation.walkthrough: 'Lost lead' paints a dog off its leash; it means POOCH losing its leading letter.
